title: Identity and pasting laws of the derived square isomorphism
statement:
Use the derived square isomorphisms $\theta^D_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ of cartesian squares $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso] (here $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, functors $\Dplus(Y_{\Et})\to\Dplus(X'_{\Et})$), and the composition and identity isomorphisms $c^D$, $e^D$ of the derived inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Outer rectangles of pasted cartesian squares are cartesian squares [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting].

1. (Identity square.) For $f:X\to Y$ and the square $\square_f=(f,f,\mathrm{id}_Y,\mathrm{id}_X)$: $\theta^D_{\square_f}=((e^D_X)^{-1}f^{-1})\circ(f^{-1}e^D_Y):f^{-1}\mathrm{id}_Y^{-1}\to f^{-1}\to\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}f^{-1}$.
2. (Horizontal pasting.) For $\square_1=(f,f',g,g')$ and a cartesian square $\square_2=(f',f'',h,h')$ with $h:Y''\to Y'$, $h':X''\to X'$, $f'':X''\to Y''$, and the outer rectangle $\square_2\cdot\square_1=(f,f'',g\circ h,g'\circ h')$:
$$
 \theta^D_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}\circ(f''^{-1}c^D_{g,h})=(c^D_{g',h'}f^{-1})\circ(h'^{-1}\theta^D_{\square_1})\circ(\theta^D_{\square_2}g^{-1}):\ f''^{-1}h^{-1}g^{-1}\to(g'h')^{-1}f^{-1}.
$$
3. (Vertical pasting.) For $\square_1$ as above and a cartesian square $\square_3=(e,e',g',g'')$ with $e:W\to X$, $e':W'\to X'$, $g'':W'\to W$, and the outer rectangle $\square_1\circ\square_3=(f\circ e,f'\circ e',g,g'')$:
$$
 \theta^D_{\square_1\circ\square_3}\circ(c^D_{f',e'}g^{-1})=(g''^{-1}c^D_{f,e})\circ(\theta^D_{\square_3}f^{-1})\circ(e'^{-1}\theta^D_{\square_1}):\ e'^{-1}f'^{-1}g^{-1}\to g''^{-1}(fe)^{-1}.
$$
The same three identities hold for the sheaf-level isomorphisms $\theta_\square$ with $c,e$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition].

proof.text: **Step 1 (sheaf level).** The three identities for the sheaf-level isomorphisms $\theta_\square=c_{f,g'}^{-1}\circ c_{g,f'}$, with $c,e$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], are [lem-weil-pbc-square-iso-pasting] (1)-(3). (They follow from the associativity and unit laws of $c,e$, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1); e.g. for (2): by associativity for $(g,h,f'')$ the left side is $c_{f,g'h'}^{-1}\circ c_{g,hf''}\circ(c_{h,f''}g^{-1})$, and by associativity for $(f,g',h')$ and $(g,f',h')$ the right side is $c_{f,g'h'}^{-1}\circ c_{fg',h'}\circ c_{gf',h'}^{-1}\circ c_{g,f'h'}\circ(c_{h,f''}g^{-1})$, equal since $fg'=gf'$ and $f'h'=hf''$.) Since $\theta_\square$, $c$, $e$ are natural, applying them degreewise to complexes gives isomorphisms of complexes satisfying the same three identities degreewise.

proof.text: **Step 2 (dictionary between termwise and derived transformations on $D$).** For each morphism of schemes $s$ let $s^{-1}_D$ be the termwise-induced functor on the unbounded derived categories with its natural isomorphism $\varphi_{s,K}:s^{-1}_D(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(s^{-1}K)$, natural in the complex $K$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] (the $\beta_s$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]); $Q$ is the localization at the quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a word $w=(s_1,\dots,s_n)$ of composable morphisms put $w_D=s^{-1}_{1,D}\circ\dots\circ s^{-1}_{n,D}$, $w^{-1}=s_1^{-1}\circ\dots\circ s_n^{-1}$ (termwise on complexes), and define $\Phi^w_K:w_D(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(w^{-1}K)$ by $\Phi^{()}_K=\mathrm{id}_{QK}$ and $\Phi^{(s,w)}_K=\varphi_{s,w^{-1}K}\circ s^{-1}_D(\Phi^w_K)$. By induction on the length of $w$, $\Phi^{w\cdot v}_K=\Phi^w_{v^{-1}K}\circ w_D(\Phi^v_K)$ for words $w,v$ (concatenation). Say that a natural transformation $\sigma:w_D\to w'_D$ *lifts* a natural transformation $\tau:w^{-1}\to w'^{-1}$ of functors on complexes if $\sigma_{QK}=(\Phi^{w'}_K)^{-1}\circ Q(\tau_K)\circ\Phi^w_K$ for every complex $K$. Then: (a) $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}$ lifts $\theta_\square$ (words $(f',g)$, $(g',f)$; $\Phi^{(f',g)}=\beta_1$, $\Phi^{(g',f)}=\beta_2$; [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]); $c^D_{u,v}$ on $D$ lifts $c_{u,v}$ (words $(v,u)$, $(uv)$) and $e^D_X$ on $D$ lifts $e_X$ (words $(\mathrm{id}_X)$, $()$) ([lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], the formulas of its Step 3). (b) If $\sigma$ lifts $\tau$ and $\sigma'$ lifts $\tau'$ (composable), $\sigma'\circ\sigma$ lifts $\tau'\circ\tau$ (the middle $\Phi$ cancels); an invertible $\sigma$ lifting an invertible $\tau$ has $\sigma^{-1}$ lifting $\tau^{-1}$; the identity lifts the identity. (c) Left whiskering: if $\sigma:w_D\to w'_D$ lifts $\tau$, then $t^{-1}_D\sigma$ lifts $t^{-1}\tau$ (words $(t,w),(t,w')$): naturality of $\varphi_t$ in the complex for the morphism $\tau_K$ gives $\varphi_{t,w'^{-1}K}\circ t^{-1}_D(Q\tau_K)=Q(t^{-1}\tau_K)\circ\varphi_{t,w^{-1}K}$, so $\Phi^{(t,w')}_K\circ t^{-1}_D(\sigma_{QK})=\varphi_{t,w'^{-1}K}\circ t^{-1}_D(Q\tau_K\circ\Phi^w_K)=Q(t^{-1}\tau_K)\circ\Phi^{(t,w)}_K$. (d) Right whiskering: if $\sigma:w_D\to w'_D$ lifts $\tau$ and $v$ is a word, then $\sigma v_D$ lifts $\tau v^{-1}$ (words $w\cdot v,w'\cdot v$): by naturality of $\sigma$ for the isomorphism $\Phi^v_K:v_D(QK)\to Q(v^{-1}K)$, $\sigma_{v_D(QK)}=w'_D(\Phi^v_K)^{-1}\circ\sigma_{Q(v^{-1}K)}\circ w_D(\Phi^v_K)=w'_D(\Phi^v_K)^{-1}\circ(\Phi^{w'}_{v^{-1}K})^{-1}\circ Q(\tau_{v^{-1}K})\circ\Phi^w_{v^{-1}K}\circ w_D(\Phi^v_K)$, which is $(\Phi^{w'\cdot v}_K)^{-1}\circ Q(\tau_{v^{-1}K})\circ\Phi^{w\cdot v}_K$ by the concatenation formula.

proof.text: **Step 3 (the identities on $D$ at the objects $QK$).** Write $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}$, $c^D$, $e^D$ for the transformations on the unbounded derived categories (Step 2 (a)). Each side of each of the three identities, read on $D$, is a composite of such transformations, their inverses, and their whiskerings by functors $t^{-1}_D$ on the left or on the right; the corresponding expression with $\theta,c,e$ in place of $\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb}},c^D,e^D$ and $t^{-1}$ in place of $t^{-1}_D$ is the corresponding side of the termwise identity. By Step 2 (a)-(d), applied factor by factor, each side on $D$ lifts the corresponding termwise side, with the same source and target words on both sides (identity (1): words $(f,\mathrm{id}_Y)$ and $(\mathrm{id}_X,f)$; (2): $(f'',h,g)$ and $(g'h',f)$; (3): $(e',f',g)$ and $(g'',fe)$). For instance the right side of (2) is $(c^D_{g',h'}f^{-1}_D)\circ(h'^{-1}_D\theta^D_{\square_1,\mathrm{unb}})\circ(\theta^D_{\square_2,\mathrm{unb}}g^{-1}_D)$, which lifts $(c_{g',h'}f^{-1})\circ(h'^{-1}\theta_{\square_1})\circ(\theta_{\square_2}g^{-1})$ by (d), (c), (d) and (b); its left side $\theta^D_{\square_2\cdot\square_1,\mathrm{unb}}\circ(f''^{-1}_Dc^D_{g,h})$ lifts $\theta_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}\circ(f''^{-1}c_{g,h})$ by (c) and (b). By Step 1 the termwise sides are equal, so at every $QK$ the two sides on $D$ are $(\Phi^{w'}_K)^{-1}\circ Q(\text{the same morphism of complexes})\circ\Phi^w_K$, hence equal.

proof.text: **Step 4 (the identities on all of $D$).** For each identity, the two sides are natural transformations between the same two functors (composites of the functors $s^{-1}_D$, from the unbounded derived category of the bottom right scheme to that of the top left scheme of the square or rectangle), being composites of whiskered natural transformations; by Step 3 they agree at every object $QK$, $K$ a complex. $Q$ is a localization at the quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so by the uniqueness clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (with $L=Q$) the two sides are equal natural transformations on $D$. This is the argument of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] Steps 5-6 and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-commshift] Step 5.

**Step 5 (restriction to $\Dplus$).** The inverse images on $\Dplus$ are the restrictions of the $s^{-1}_D$ to the full subcategories $\Dplus$, which they preserve [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; $\theta^D_\square$ on $\Dplus$ is the restriction of $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso], and $c^D$, $e^D$ on $\Dplus$ are the restrictions of the transformations on $D$ ([lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] Step 4 and the uniqueness in its clause (2)). Whiskering and composing natural transformations commute with restriction to full subcategories preserved by the functors, so each side of each identity on $\Dplus$ is the restriction of the corresponding side on $D$, and the identities of Step 4 restrict to the three identities of the statement.
